layout.title: Sign in
layout.description: Log in to your work tools and profile.

login.title: Login to your account
login.description: Sign in with your email or username and password.
login.verifyEmailAfterSignup: Check your inbox for a verification link. You must verify your email before signing in.
login.lastUsedHintEmail: You last signed in with email and password.
login.lastUsedHintUsername: You last signed in with username and password.
login.lastUsedHintPasskey: You last signed in with a passkey.
login.lastUsedHintEmailCode: You last signed in with a code sent by email.

errors.emailNotVerified: Please verify your email first. Can't find the link? Ask for a new one below.
errors.signInFailed: Could not sign in. Check your details and try again.
errors.passkeyFailed: Passkey sign-in failed. Try again or use your password.

resend.title: Didn't get the email?
resend.description: Enter your email and we'll send you a new verification link.
resend.sent: If an unverified account uses this address, a new link is on its way. Check your inbox and spam folder.
resend.error: Could not send the email. Try again in a minute.

login.addAccountDescription: Accounts already signed in on this browser stay signed in.

emailCode.title: Sign in with a code
emailCode.description: We'll email a 6-digit code to the address on your account. Read it on any device, then type it here.
emailCode.sent: If an account uses {email}, a 6-digit code is on its way. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
emailCode.newCode: Didn't get it? Send a new code

errors.invalidCode: That code isn't right. Check it and try again.
errors.expired: This code has expired. Ask for a new one.
errors.tooManyAttempts: Too many wrong codes. Ask for a new one.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.sendFailed: Could not send the code. Try again in a minute.
errors.signInFailed: Could not sign in. Try again.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor authentication
twoFactor.descriptionTotp: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
twoFactor.descriptionBackup: Enter one of your backup codes. Each code works once.
twoFactor.trustDeviceHint: You won’t be asked for a code on this device. Only choose this on a device you own.
twoFactor.expiredDescription: This sign-in expired or had too many wrong codes. Sign in with your password again.

errors.invalidCode: That code is not valid. Enter the current code from your app.
errors.invalidBackupCode: That backup code is not valid or was already used.
errors.locked: Too many wrong codes. Try again in 15 minutes.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a few seconds and try again.
errors.failed: Could not verify the code. Try again.

forgotPassword.title: Reset your password
forgotPassword.description: Enter the email on your account. If it exists, we will send you a link to choose a new password.
forgotPassword.emailHint: Use the same email you registered with. If you usually sign in with a username, recovery still uses your account email.
forgotPassword.emailSent: If an account exists for that email, you will receive a reset link shortly.

errors.requestFailed: Could not send the reset email. Try again.

resetPassword.title: Choose a new password
resetPassword.description: Enter and confirm your new password below.
resetPassword.invalidTokenDescription: This reset link is no longer valid. Request a new one to continue.
resetPassword.missingTokenDescription: Open the link from your email, or request a new password reset.
resetPassword.passwordHint: Must be at least 8 characters long.
resetPassword.success: Your password was updated. You can sign in now.

errors.resetFailed: Could not reset your password. Try again or request a new link.

signup.title: Create an account
signup.description: Enter your information below to create your account
signup.usernameHint: 3-30 characters: letters, numbers, dots, and underscores only.
signup.usernameInvalidHint: Use only letters, numbers, dots, and underscores.
signup.emailDescription: We'll use this to contact you. We will not share your email with anyone else.
signup.passwordHint: Must be at least 8 characters long.
signup.afterRegisterRedirect: Account created. Check your email to verify before signing in.

errors.signUpFailed: Could not create your account. Try again.
errors.compromisedPassword: This password appears in known data breaches. Choose a different one.
errors.usernameTooShort: Username must be at least 3 characters.
errors.usernameTaken: That username is already taken. Try another.

screen.headline: One account for <accent>all your apps</accent>.
screen.subhead: Sign in once and reach every app connected to {name}. Your profile and security settings follow you everywhere.

social.error: Could not sign in with that account. Try again or use another method.
social.notLinked: That account isn't connected to a {name} account yet. Sign in another way, then connect it from your security settings.
social.noEmail: That account didn't share an email address. Try again later or sign in another way.
social.signUpDisabled: There's no account for that address yet, and this sign-in method can't create one. Sign in another way.

app.signUp: Create your account to continue to <app>{name}</app>
app.unverifiedHint: {name} has not reviewed it: only continue if you trust it.

consent.emptyDescription: There is no pending OAuth request. Start the flow from the application you want to connect.
consent.intro: This application is requesting access to your account. Review the permissions below before continuing.

errors.needSignIn: You need to sign in before you can approve this request.

consent.defaultScopes: Default permissions for this client (no explicit scopes in the request).

scopes.offline_access: Access when you are not actively using the application

unverified.title: Unverified app
unverified.dynamic: This app registered itself and has not been reviewed. Only allow it if you trust it and started this sign-in yourself.
unverified.metadataDocument: This app identifies itself with a document on {host} and has not been reviewed. Only allow it if you trust it and started this sign-in yourself.
unverified.redirect: If you allow, you will be sent to {host}.

overview.title: Overview

activity.title: Sign-in activity
activity.description: Sign-ins, new accounts and sign-outs per day, last 30 days.
activity.note: Sign-outs are tracked from October 6, 2026. Earlier sign-ins only include sessions that were still active then.

overview.description: Accounts, sign-in activity and the newest members of the platform.

recentUsers.title: Recently joined
recentUsers.description: The newest accounts. Open one to see its sessions and activity.

stats.error: Could not load one or more metrics. Ensure you are signed in as an admin.

admins.title: Administrators
admins.hint: Accounts with access to this console.

banned.title: Banned
banned.hint: Accounts that can't sign in right now.

verified.title: Verified email
verified.hint: Accounts that confirmed their email address.

recent.title: New (7 days)
recent.hint: Accounts created in the last 7 days.

applications.title: Applications
applications.description: OAuth clients that can sign people in with {name}: their redirect URLs, grant types and consent settings.
applications.unusedHint: {count, plural, one {# application hasn’t} other {# applications haven’t}} been used in the last 30 days.

panel.selfRegisteredHint: Registered itself: not reviewed by an admin
panel.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, client ID, redirect URI, or grant…
panel.empty: No OAuth clients for this account yet.
panel.footnote: Data from {getClients}. Register and edit (including {skipConsent}) call {create} and {update}; other mutations use {deleteClient} and {rotateSecret}. See the OAuth provider docs. Clients are scoped to the signed-in user (or {clientReference} when configured). Self-registered clients have no owner and are all listed; they can be disabled or deleted, not edited.

registration.title: Self-registration
registration.description: Lets MCP clients and AI agents register themselves instead of being added here. They only get the scopes below, always show the consent screen marked as unverified, and never get machine (client credentials) access.

signed_in.label: Signed-in users only
signed_in.hint: Only requests carrying a user's session may register. Most MCP clients cannot.

open.label: Anyone (open registration)
open.hint: What MCP clients expect: any app may register, then each user approves it on the consent screen.

registration.missingScope: No longer a scope of this server: ignored
registration.endpoint: Registration endpoint: {url} (advertised in the discovery document).
registration.saved: Settings saved. The auth server applies them within a minute.
registration.dialogDescription: Clients that register themselves are not reviewed. People see them as unverified apps and approve each one on the consent screen.
registration.cimdHint: The client_id is an HTTPS URL to the app's JSON metadata, as newer MCP clients use. Only public hosts are fetched, without redirects, 5 KB at most.
registration.hostsHint: One per line. Empty: any public HTTPS host.
registration.scopesHint: Each user still approves the scopes an app asks for. Removing a scope also removes it from clients already registered; tokens already issued keep it until they expire.
registration.perHourHint: Across every instance, for both methods. Each address is also limited to 5 registrations a minute.

branding.title: Sign-in branding
branding.description: How the sign-in screens look when people arrive from <app>{client}</app>: login, sign-up, two-factor, password reset and consent. The {brand} mark stays visible on every screen.
branding.logoFetchedOnSave: The server fetches the logo when you save; the preview shows it then.
branding.accentInvalid: Enter the accent as a hex color such as {example}.
branding.hexInvalid: Enter a hex color such as {example}.
branding.displayNameHint: Shown as “Sign in to continue to …”. Empty uses the application name.
branding.accentOff: Off: the screens keep the theme’s colors.

contrast.label: Contrast checks
contrast.textAdjusted: Text in the accent uses {color} to reach {min}:1.

branding.logoAppIconHint: The icon found for the app (its {field} or its site), as on the consent screen.
branding.logoUrlHint: https on a public host. {name} fetches and caches it; browsers never load it from there.
branding.logoFileHint: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, ICO or SVG, up to 256 KB. Square works best.
branding.panelHint: Headline and background image of the dark panel. PNG, JPEG, WebP or AVIF, up to 1 MB.
branding.social: Social sign-in on this app’s screens
branding.socialHint: Hides buttons on this app’s screens only; it does not stop anyone from signing in another way.
branding.faintOnLight: Buttons in this color barely stand out from the light card (WCAG asks 3:1 for controls). Labels stay readable; consider a darker shade.
branding.faintOnDark: Buttons in this color barely stand out from the dark card (WCAG asks 3:1 for controls). Labels stay readable; consider a lighter shade.

registration.unknownScope: "{scope}" is not a scope of this server.
registration.invalidHost: "{raw}" is not a host name, e.g. {example}.
registration.invalidLimit: The hourly limit must be a whole number from 0 to {max}.
registration.notSelfRegistered: Only self-registered clients can be changed here.

branding.logoMissing: Choose a logo file to upload.
branding.logoFetchFailed: Could not fetch an image at the logo URL. Check that it is public and is an image.
branding.faintOnLight: The accent is faint on the light card: buttons will barely stand out.
branding.faintOnDark: The accent is faint on the dark card: buttons will barely stand out.

register.title: Register OAuth application
register.description: Creates a client tied to your account via {endpoint} (trusted apps can set {field}). See Better Auth, Create client.
register.redirectUrisHintPublic: One per line or comma-separated. HTTPS, or http on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1].
register.redirectUrisHintConfidential: One per line or comma-separated. HTTPS only, localhost included. For local development, register a separate public client.
register.redirectUrisRequired: Enter at least one redirect URI (one per line or comma-separated).
register.deviceCodeHint: Adds the device code grant (RFC 8628): the app shows a code and the user approves it at {path} on another screen. Usually a public client.
register.skipConsentHint: Users will not see the consent screen for this application. Use only for first-party or fully trusted integrations.
register.successWithSecret: Copy the client secret now, it may only be shown once.
register.successPublic: Public client, no secret is issued. Use PKCE at the token endpoint.

rowActions.editHint: Name, redirect URIs, device sign-in and skip consent
rowActions.brandingHint: Logo, accent color and wording of the sign-in screens for this app

editDialog.title: Edit application
editDialog.description: Updates {clientId} via {endpoint} (restricted fields such as {field}). See Better Auth, Update client.
editDialog.redirectUrisHint: One per line or comma-separated. HTTPS required. Only public clients may use http on localhost.
editDialog.redirectUrisRequired: Enter at least one redirect URI (one per line or comma-separated).
editDialog.deviceCodeHint: Allows the device code grant. Turning it off stops new device sign-ins; tokens already issued keep working.
editDialog.skipConsentHint: When enabled, users are not prompted to approve scopes for this application.

deleteDialog.title: Delete application?
deleteDialog.description: Permanently removes {name} ({clientId}). OAuth tokens and consents for this client may be affected.

rotateDialog.title: Rotate client secret?
rotateDialog.description: The previous secret stops working immediately. Save the new secret somewhere safe, it may only be shown once.
rotateDialog.newSecretIssued: New client secret issued, copy it now

selfRegistered.disableDescription: It can no longer sign anyone in or refresh its tokens. Access tokens already issued work until they expire (an hour at most).
selfRegistered.deleteDescriptionMetadataDocument: Its tokens and the consents people gave it are deleted too. A metadata-document client is created again the next time it signs someone in. To block it, disable it instead.
selfRegistered.deleteDescriptionDynamic: Its tokens and the consents people gave it are deleted too. The app can register again while dynamic registration is on.

brandingErrors.displayNameTooLong: Display name: Keep it under {max} characters.
brandingErrors.panelTextTooLong: Side panel text: Keep it under {max} characters.
brandingErrors.accentColor: Accent color: enter a hex color such as {example}.
brandingErrors.logoSource: Choose where the logo comes from.
brandingErrors.logoUrl: Logo URL: enter an https URL on a public host (default port).
brandingErrors.logoTooLarge: The logo must be 256 KB or smaller.
brandingErrors.logoType: The logo must be a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, ICO or SVG image.
brandingErrors.panelImageEmpty: The side panel image is empty.
brandingErrors.panelImageTooLarge: The side panel image must be 1 MB or smaller.
brandingErrors.panelImageType: The side panel image must be a PNG, JPEG, WebP or AVIF image.

apis.title: APIs
apis.description: Your APIs (protected resources) that accept {name} access tokens: the scopes clients can request, which applications can use them, and their token settings.

tokenSettings.lifetimePositive: {field, select, access {The access token lifetime must be a positive number of minutes.} other {The refresh token lifetime must be a positive number of days.}}
tokenSettings.lifetimeMinimum: {field, select, access {The access token lifetime} other {The refresh token lifetime}} must be at least one minute.
tokenSettings.lifetimeMaximum: {field, select, access {The access token lifetime can be at most {max} minutes, the server default.} other {The refresh token lifetime can be at most {max} days, the server default.}}
tokenSettings.claimsInvalidJson: Custom claims must be valid JSON, e.g. {example}.
tokenSettings.claimsNotObject: Custom claims must be a JSON object, e.g. {example}.
tokenSettings.claimsEmptyName: A custom claim name cannot be empty.
tokenSettings.claimsReserved: {count, plural, one {{claims} is a reserved claim: the server sets it.} other {{claims} are reserved claims: the server sets them.}} Reserved: {reserved}.
tokenSettings.claimsTooLarge: Custom claims are too large ({kilobytes} KB at most): they are added to every token.

errors.reservedScope: "{scope}" is an OpenID Connect scope, available to every client already.
errors.invalidIdentifier: The identifier must be an absolute URL without a fragment, e.g. {example}.
errors.authServerCannotBeDisabled: The auth server itself cannot be disabled.
errors.deleteFromEnv: This API is set in {variable} and would come back on the next deploy. Disable it instead.
errors.authServerStaysOpen: The auth server stays open to every application: signing in depends on it.
errors.accessFailed: Could not change which applications can use the API.
errors.tokensFailed: Could not save the token settings.

apis.restrictLabel: Only issue these scopes for this API
apis.restrictHint: Tokens for this API carry only these scopes (and the OpenID Connect ones). Off: they carry every scope the client was granted.

register.title: Register an API
register.description: Clients ask for a token for it with the {param} parameter. The token's audience is the identifier, and the API verifies it against the JWKS.
register.identifierHint: Usually the API's base URL. It cannot be changed later.
register.scopesHint: Separated by spaces or commas. Machine clients ({grant}) must be limited to some of them.

list.description: New and changed scopes reach the auth server within a minute. Access and token settings apply to the next token.
list.envScopesText: Available to every client, whichever API it calls: <mono>{scopes}</mono>. To manage them here, add them to the API they belong to, then remove the variable.

item.noResourceParam: Tokens issued without a resource parameter.
item.noneLinked: None linked: no application can get tokens

edit.title: Edit {name}
edit.scopesHint: Removing a scope does not change clients that already have it, but no new token carries it.
edit.disabledHint: No new tokens for this API. Tokens already issued work until they expire.

access.title: Applications that can use {name}
access.allHint: Any application can get tokens for this API, within its scopes.
access.linkedHint: Other applications are refused ({error}), including when they refresh a token.
access.filterPlaceholder: Filter by name or client ID
access.linksHintAll: Links only matter once the API is limited to linked applications. A linked application can also introspect this API's tokens.
access.linksHintLinked: A linked application can also introspect this API's tokens.
access.noneLinkedWarning: No application is linked: none can get tokens for this API.

tokens.title: Token settings for {name}
tokens.description: Applied to every access token issued for this API. Tokens already issued keep their settings.
tokens.accessTtlHint: Default: {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. Can only be shorter.
tokens.refreshTtlHint: Default: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Can only be shorter.
tokens.claimsHint: A JSON object added to every access token for this API. Reserved: <mono>{claims}</mono>.
tokens.dpopHint: Clients must send a DPoP proof to get a token for this API, and the token is bound to their key. The API must check the proof on each request.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.description: Clients can no longer get tokens for it, and the tokens already issued for it stop working at once. To stop new tokens only, disable it instead.

signInProviders.title: Sign-in providers
signInProviders.description: Let people sign in to {name} with Google, Apple, Microsoft and 30+ other accounts.

panel.activeDescription: In this order on the sign-in and sign-up pages, and under Connected accounts in each user's dashboard. Changes reach the sign-in page within 30 seconds.
panel.noneActive: No provider is on. Pick one in the list to set it up.
panel.connectedAccounts: {count, plural, one {# connected account} other {# connected accounts}}
panel.providersDescription: Every provider Better Auth supports. Create an OAuth app with the provider, register the callback URL shown in its settings, then paste the credentials. Secrets are stored encrypted and never shown again.
panel.environmentDescription: Set by environment variables ({clientIdVar} and {clientSecretVar}): change them there, or remove them to manage this provider here.
panel.defaultNote: Create an OAuth app with {name}, register the callback URL below, then paste its credentials.
panel.callbackHint: Also called redirect URI or return URL.
panel.secretsUnreadable: The stored secrets cannot be decrypted ({envVar} has changed). Enter them again.
panel.buttonNameHint: Shown as "Continue with …" on the sign-in page.
panel.allowSignUpHint: Off: only people who already have an account can sign in with it (connected from their dashboard, or with the same verified email).
panel.oneTapHint: Google's own sign-in prompt, at the top of the sign-in and sign-up pages, for people already signed in to Google in their browser. Uses this client ID: add {origin} to its Authorized JavaScript origins in the Google Cloud console. Only while Google is on.
panel.enabledHint: Off: the button disappears and sign-ins with this provider are refused. Settings are kept.

errors.envManaged: This provider is set by environment variables. Change them, or remove them to manage it here.
errors.appleKeyNotEc: Private key: expected the EC (P-256) key downloaded from Apple (.p8).
errors.appleKeyInvalid: Private key: not a valid PEM private key. Paste the whole .p8 file, BEGIN and END lines included.
errors.issuerNotHttps: The URL must start with https://.
errors.salesforceDomain: My Domain: a host name such as example.my.salesforce.com.
errors.cognitoRegion: Region: an AWS region such as eu-west-1.
errors.googleHd: Workspace domain: a domain such as example.com.
errors.missingFields: Fill in {fields} before turning it on.

apple.note: Apple needs an HTTPS return URL on a real domain (no localhost) and sends the user back with a POST.

clientId.label: Services ID
clientId.hint: The identifier of a Services ID with Sign in with Apple turned on, e.g. com.example.signin.

keyId.label: Key ID
keyId.hint: A key with Sign in with Apple enabled.

privateKey.label: Private key (.p8)
privateKey.hint: The client secret is a JWT signed with this key; it is generated and renewed automatically.

appBundleIdentifier.label: App bundle ID
appBundleIdentifier.hint: Only for native iOS sign-in (ID tokens issued to your app instead of the Services ID).

clientSecret.label: Client secret
clientSecret.hint: Leave empty for a public client (PKCE only).

clientSecret.label: App client secret
clientSecret.hint: Only if the app client has a secret.

github.note: An OAuth App works as is. A GitHub App also needs the account permission Email addresses set to Read-only, or sign-in fails with no email.

hd.label: Workspace domain
hd.hint: Only accept accounts of this Google Workspace domain.

clientSecret.label: Client secret
clientSecret.hint: Only if client secret is turned on for the app.

tenantId.label: Tenant
tenantId.hint: common (any account), organizations, consumers, or your directory (tenant) ID to allow only your organization.

paypal.note: Turn on "Log in with PayPal" for the app and ask for the email address.

loginUrl.label: My Domain
loginUrl.hint: Host name only. Replaces login.salesforce.com or test.salesforce.com.

twitter.note: Use the OAuth 2.0 credentials (not the API key) and ask for email access in the app's settings.

wechat.note: Website application (QR code sign-in). WeChat returns no email address.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Keys people create for their scripts to call your APIs: turn them on or off, set their maximum lifetime, and revoke any key.

allKeys.title: All keys
allKeys.description: Newest first{truncated, select, true {, the latest {limit}} other {}}. Expired keys are deleted the next time keys are used or created. Banning or deleting an account revokes its keys; deleting an organization deletes its keys (keys an organization owns stay when the member who created them leaves).

settings.description: People create keys from their account page for one of your APIs and some of its scopes. The API checks each key with this server. A key never signs anyone in to this server or the admin console.
settings.statusOff: Off: no new keys, and every key is refused
settings.apisNone: None: register an API with scopes, open to every application
settings.verifyEndpoint: Verification endpoint: {endpoint}. The API authenticates as an application registered here, linked to that API (APIs page, Access). APIs limited to linked applications do not accept keys.

dialog.description: Keys are long-lived: prefer short lifetimes. Lowering the maximum applies to new keys only.
dialog.allowHint: Off: nobody can create a key and every existing key is refused at verification. Keys are kept, and work again when you turn this back on.
dialog.saved: Settings saved. The auth server applies them within a minute.

table.revokeOrgDescription: This key of the organization {owner} stops working right away. Its owners and admins can create a new one if API keys are on.
table.revokeUserDescription: The key of {owner} stops working right away. They can create a new one if API keys are on.

errors.chooseEnabled: Choose whether API keys are on.
errors.maxLifetimeRange: The maximum lifetime must be a whole number of days from 1 to {max}.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: Signed HTTPS notifications that tell your apps when {name} users, roles and organization memberships change.

eventDescriptions.user_created: An account is created (sign-up, admin, SSO, SCIM).
eventDescriptions.user_updated: Name, email, email verification, username or picture changes.
eventDescriptions.user_banned: An account is banned, or deactivated by SCIM.
eventDescriptions.user_unbanned: A ban is lifted, or SCIM reactivates the account.
eventDescriptions.organization_member_removed: Someone leaves or is removed from an organization.
eventDescriptions.organization_member_role_changed: A member's role in an organization changes.

add.title: Add an endpoint
add.description: Ostiary POSTs a signed JSON event to this URL when one of the chosen events happens, and retries for about a day if it fails.
add.urlHintLocalhost: HTTPS, on a public address. {url} is accepted ({envVar}, development only).

list.title: Endpoints
list.description: Every request carries the {id}, {timestamp} and {signature} headers (Standard Webhooks). An endpoint that fails {count, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} in a row is disabled.

created.title: Endpoint added
created.description: Copy the signing secret into the app at {url}: it verifies each delivery with it. It is not shown again.

item.disabledNotice: Disabled after {count, plural, one {# failed attempt} other {# failed attempts}} in a row. Fix the receiver, then turn it back on: pending events are sent again.
item.disabledNoticeOn: Disabled on {date} after {count, plural, one {# failed attempt} other {# failed attempts}} in a row. Fix the receiver, then turn it back on: pending events are sent again.

edit.title: Edit endpoint
edit.enabledHint: While disabled, new events are not recorded for this endpoint and retries wait.

rotate.title: Regenerate the signing secret?
rotate.description: Deliveries are signed with both the old and the new secret for 24 hours, so the app can switch without missing events.
rotate.newDescription: Copy it into the app now: it is not shown again. For the next 24 hours, deliveries carry a signature with the old secret too.

delete.title: Delete this endpoint?
delete.description: {url} stops receiving events, and its delivery log and pending retries are deleted. To pause it, disable it instead.

log.disabled: Disabled: retries wait until it is turned back on.
log.empty: No delivery yet. Use “Send test event” on the Webhooks page to try the endpoint.
log.footer: The latest {shown} deliveries. Deliveries are kept {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. A failed delivery is retried {retries, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} over about a day; “Redeliver” sends the same event (same {header}) again now.

errors.disabledTest: The endpoint is disabled: turn it on to send a test event.
errors.testNotSent: The test event could not be sent.
errors.disabledRedeliver: The endpoint is disabled: turn it on to redeliver.
errors.eventNotSent: The event could not be sent.

users.title: Users
users.description: Find accounts, change roles, ban or remove them, and open an account to see its sessions and activity.

list.poweredBy: Powered by listUsers, createUser, setRole, updateUser, setUserPassword, and related methods from the Better Auth admin plugin. You must be signed in as an admin.

rowActions.editDescription: Change the name or email address. A new email address must be verified by the user before they can sign in again.
rowActions.name: Name
rowActions.passwordDescription: Sets a new password for {email} using setUserPassword.
rowActions.removeDescription: This permanently deletes {name} ({email}) and everything linked to the account. Audit log entries are kept without their name or email. This cannot be undone.

detailActions.signOutError: Could not sign this user out.
detailActions.signedOut: Signed out of {count, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}
detailActions.exportError: Could not export this user's data.
detailActions.exported: Data exported. The export is recorded in the audit log.
detailActions.impersonateDescription: You will see the account dashboard exactly as this user does, for up to an hour. A banner there lets you stop and return. This is recorded in the audit log.
detailActions.signOutDescription: Every session of this user ends now, on every device. They will need to sign in again.
detailActions.resetTwoFactorDescription: Their authenticator app, backup codes and trusted devices stop working, and they sign in with their password alone until they set it up again. Only do this once you have confirmed who is asking. This is recorded in the audit log.

detail.scimDescription: The identity provider manages this account. Remove the user there: deleting the account here does not stop the directory from creating it again on its next sync. The user cannot delete the account from their dashboard.

sessions.title: Active sessions
sessions.description: Devices where this account is signed in.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.description: Keys this account created for scripts. Banning or deleting the account revokes them.

organizations.title: Organizations
organizations.empty: Not a member of any organization.

consent.title: Consent
consent.description: Permissions people have granted to OAuth clients, with the scopes and when they were given.

panel.searchPlaceholder: Search by user, client, consent id, reference, or scope…
panel.emptyNone: No consents recorded for this account yet.
panel.footnote: Data from {getConsents}; client names resolved via {getClients}. Revoke uses {deleteConsent}. See OAuth consent in the OAuth provider docs. The interactive authorize UI is at {path}.

rowActions.dialogDescription: Removes this user's grant for {client} ({clientId}). The client may need to request authorization again.

usage.title: App usage

signingKeys.title: Signing keys
signingKeys.description: The keys {name} signs ID tokens and JWT access tokens with. Apps and APIs verify tokens against the public keys published in the JWKS.

rotation.title: Automatic rotation
rotation.description: Replaces the signing key on a schedule. A retired key stays in the JWKS for the grace period, so tokens it signed keep verifying.
rotation.every: Every {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
rotation.graceValue: {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after a key retires
rotation.dialogDescription: A new key is created when the current one reaches the interval. Apps that cache the JWKS fetch it again when they see the new key id.
rotation.intervalHint: Changing the interval also applies to the current key: it retires when it reaches the new age, or at the next token if it is already older.
rotation.graceHint: How long a retired key stays published. Keep it longer than your longest token lifetime (access tokens: 1 hour, ID tokens: 10 hours).
rotation.saved: Settings saved. The auth server applies them within a minute.

keys.title: Keys
keys.description: Private keys are stored encrypted and never shown.
keys.empty: No key yet. The first one is created when the first token is signed, or when you rotate.

rotate.title: Rotate the signing key now?
rotate.newKey: A new key signs every token from now on.
rotate.caching: Apps and APIs that cache the JWKS pick up the new key automatically: they fetch the JWKS again when they meet its key id.
rotate.oldTokens: Tokens signed with the current key stay valid until they expire: the key stays published for the grace period ({grace}).
rotate.compromised: If the key may have leaked, rotate now, then choose a short grace period: a retired key verifies tokens for as long as it is published.
rotate.done: Key rotated. New tokens use key {kid}.

errors.interval: Choose one of the rotation intervals offered.
errors.grace: Choose one of the grace periods offered.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.description: Connect your organization's identity provider (OIDC or SAML 2.0) so members can sign in with their work account.
sso.registerDescription: Your identity provider must redirect back to the callback URL shown below.
sso.domainHint: Users with this email domain are sent to this provider.
sso.callbackTitle: Callback URL to configure in your identity provider
sso.signInDescription: Enter your work email. We'll redirect you to your organization's identity provider.
sso.signInError: Could not start single sign-on for this address.
sso.signInFailed: Single sign-on did not complete. Try again, or ask your administrator to check the identity provider settings.

saml.registerDescription: The identity provider posts signed SAML assertions to the ACS URL below. Sign-in starts from Ostiary (SP-initiated).
saml.metadataUrlHint: The server fetches it once when you save. After a certificate rotation, fetch it again from Edit.
saml.metadataXmlHint: The EntityDescriptor your identity provider exports.
saml.ssoUrlHint: The URL for the HTTP-Redirect binding.
saml.certificateHint: PEM (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----) or its base64 body.
saml.mappingHint: First and last name are used when the identity provider sends them, otherwise the display name. The user ID is the assertion's NameID: configure a persistent identifier.
saml.wantAssertionsSignedHint: Recommended. When off, the whole response must still be signed: unsigned responses are always refused.
saml.requestSigningNote: Ostiary does not sign authentication requests: leave request signing off in the identity provider.
saml.spTitle: Values to enter in your identity provider
saml.acsUrl: ACS URL (single sign-on URL, reply URL)
saml.oktaStep1: In the Okta admin console: Applications, Create App Integration, SAML 2.0.
saml.oktaStep2: Single sign-on URL: the ACS URL. Audience URI (SP Entity ID): the SP entity ID. Name ID format: Persistent. Application username: Email.
saml.oktaStep3: Attribute statements: email = user.email, firstName = user.firstName, lastName = user.lastName (the Okta preset).
saml.oktaStep4: Assign people, then copy the metadata URL from the Sign On tab into Ostiary.
saml.entraStep1: In Microsoft Entra ID: Enterprise applications, New application, Create your own application (non-gallery), then Single sign-on, SAML.
saml.entraStep2: Basic SAML configuration: Identifier (Entity ID) = the SP entity ID, Reply URL = the ACS URL.
saml.entraStep3: Keep the default claims (the Entra ID preset). The default signing option, Sign SAML assertion, works.
saml.entraStep4: Assign users and groups, then copy the App Federation Metadata URL into Ostiary.
saml.spInitiatedNote: Only sign-in started from Ostiary is supported. Point app tiles in the identity provider's portal to {url}.
saml.detailsDescription: Enter these values in the identity provider.
saml.assertionsSignedOff: Signed responses are required (assertions may be unsigned).
saml.certExpired: The signing certificate has expired: sign-ins will fail until the IdP metadata is updated.
saml.editDescription: Changing the domain means it must be verified again. The SP entity ID and ACS URL stay the same.
saml.replaceIdp: Replace the identity provider configuration (new metadata or certificate)
